MacroMicro returned 403 in this run, so its Sep 9 verified credit-spread readings are retained only as dated references with lower freshness. Federal Reserve H.15, EIA September STEO, official ISM and current Reuters reporting control the fresh packet. The retired legacy macro dashboard is not used.
regime: $100+ Brent and acute refined-product/shipping stress are colliding with 4.8% nominal and 2.4% real US long yields. At the same time EIA confirms record electricity demand from data centres and manufacturing. The result is an inflationary physical-capex expansion in which pricing power, funded demand, balance-sheet quality and cash conversion matter more than headline growth.

channels.label: Growth / Demand
channels.regime: Nominal activity resilient, real demand uneven
channels.interpretation: Services and power demand remain strong, but $100+ oil, food inflation and high borrowing costs squeeze real household and weaker-company demand.

channels.label: Policy Relief
channels.regime: Inflation shock leaves little room for relief
channels.interpretation: Oil above $100, tight distillates and high ISM prices raise the hurdle for near-term easing even if underlying employment breadth is mixed.

channels.label: Financial Conditions
channels.interpretation: Fed H.15 shows 10Y 4.80%, 30Y 5.25% and real10Y 2.43%. This is directly hostile to leveraged project finance and distant-cash-flow equity duration.

channels.label: Broad Credit
channels.regime: Available to quality, expensive at the margin
channels.interpretation: High-quality capital remains available, but current risk-free yields and large AI/project-finance needs raise hurdle rates. Today's exact spread snapshot is not refreshed.

channels.label: Weak-End Credit Stress
channels.regime: Elevated weak-borrower stress, dated spread tick
channels.interpretation: The prior verified CCC OAS of 10.55pp remains a strong weak-end warning. Because MacroMicro was unavailable today, treat the exact spread as dated rather than live.

channels.label: Consumer
channels.interpretation: Record-near fuel costs, rising food pressure in Asia and expensive credit reduce discretionary flexibility even without a broad consumer collapse.

channels.label: Housing
channels.interpretation: A 4.8% 10Y and 5.25% 30Y keep housing and leveraged property activity under pressure.

channels.label: Industrial / AI / Power Capex
channels.interpretation: EIA forecasts record US electricity sales driven by data centres and manufacturing. Prefer actual energised capacity, orders, signed leases/PPAs and funded backlog over proposed megawatts.

channels.label: Input Costs
channels.regime: Severe energy, copper and logistics inflation
channels.interpretation: Oil/products, copper, freight, electrical components and weather-related food pressure overlap. Pricing power and contract pass-through are essential.

channels.label: Labour
channels.regime: Payroll resilience vs survey hiring weakness
channels.interpretation: Recent payroll data are resilient while ISM Services Employment remains below 50. Treat the labour picture as mixed, not uniformly hot.

channels.label: Risk Appetite
channels.regime: AI pockets resilient, broad tape pressured by oil/rates
channels.interpretation: Major US indices fell Sep 9 while selected AI names rallied. Dispersion is high and the long-yield hurdle remains restrictive.

channels.label: Crude
channels.interpretation: Brent settled $101.21 after the largest recent wave of tanker attacks. EIA's 2027 normalization path is the key medium-term counterweight.

channels.label: Refined Products
channels.interpretation: EIA expects distillate inventories below 100m barrels and below the five-year low through much of 2027, reinforcing diesel/refining/logistics scarcity.

channels.label: US Gas / Global LNG
channels.regime: Strategic LNG diversification with US supply growth
channels.interpretation: EIA sees US LNG exports rising from 17.4 bcfd in 2026 to 18.6 in 2027. Contracted US LNG benefits from diversification, while spot-price spikes can still destroy price-sensitive demand.

channels.label: Gold / Monetary Hedge
channels.regime: Strategic hedge strengthening, tactical yield conflict
channels.interpretation: Gold and silver strengthened despite high nominal yields. PPI/CPI and the real-yield response remain the tactical gate.

channels.label: Copper / Industrial Metals
channels.interpretation: Record prices validate power/grid demand and supply tightness, but softer China private-credit transmission argues against treating copper as broad China reflation.

channels.label: Battery Storage / Lithium
channels.interpretation: Peak-load and grid needs support storage/VPP deployment while excess battery manufacturing keeps commodity cell/lithium economics selective.

channels.label: Agriculture / Fertilizer Inputs
channels.interpretation: Nitrogen/feedstock pressure is now joined by Black Sea grain rerouting and early super-El Nino stress. Premium genetics/nitrogen remain less deferrable than machinery/irrigation.
